{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mt-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ed80992b4e43c7f8a050578d240d57a1b98b2662a98b5d0b050be7e5b2c602e3","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mt-class-d:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"35425fc1b75886d4bce9129f5de9443ae8cee634cff4a62363bbcd7cc017fe32","source_liveness_sha256":"bf7b5d7e97593e3a1c6181f4785c9171cedac6e24ab65da907a644a4b4907add"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Signs, work zones and school zones","heading":"C — Signs, work zones and school zones","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Signs, work zones and school zones

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic-sign shape and color both help a driver recognize a sign and the action it requires. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
In poor visibility such as fog, a driver may be able to recognize only the sign’s shape. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A02
Drivers must recognize and obey traffic signs, signals and roadway markings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A02
Traffic signs are grouped by function as regulatory, warning or information-guide signs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A02
Red traffic-control signs convey stop, yield, do not enter or wrong-way instructions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A02
The stop sign has eight sides and requires a full stop before the intersection, with yielding to traffic close enough to be an immediate hazard. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A02
If a stop-controlled intersection has a crosswalk, stop before entering that crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A02
At a yield sign, reduce to a reasonable speed and yield to every vehicle on the roadway you are joining. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A02
Do not enter a roadway marked Do Not Enter; it may be one-way or closed to all vehicle traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A02
A black arrow or symbol crossed by a red circle and slash prohibits the action pictured. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A03
Regulatory signs give required actions or maximum travel speeds, and drivers must obey their rules. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A03
The regulatory signs described in this section are rectangular with black lettering or symbols on white. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A03
Within a Do Not Pass area, do not pass a vehicle traveling in your direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A03
After passing a Pass With Care sign, passing other vehicles is permitted again when done carefully. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A03
A No U Turn sign prohibits reversing direction at that intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A03
A No Left Turn sign prohibits a left turn at that intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A03
A Keep Right sign directs traffic to the right side of an obstruction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A03
A posted speed-limit sign sets the maximum speed from its location until another speed-limit sign changes it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A03
Limited nighttime visibility may require a speed below the posted maximum. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A03
A Speed Zone Ahead sign warns that a reduced speed limit is approaching. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A04
Warning signs use black and yellow and generally have a diamond shape. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A04
The railroad-crossing-ahead warning is round and is the only round warning traffic sign described by the handbook. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A04
A Crossroad warning indicates a four-way intersection and calls for watching traffic entering across the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A04
A Winding Road sign warns of a sequence of turns or curves ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A04
At a T-intersection warning, the road ahead does not continue straight and turns right and left. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A04
An angled Side Road sign warns of a side road joining the highway at an angle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A04
The right-side Side Road sign warns of a roadway joining from the right. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A04
A Sharp Right Turn warning identifies a sharp right turn ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A04
A Sharp Left and Right Turn warning identifies a sharp left turn followed by a sharp right turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A04
A Right and Left Curves warning identifies a right curve followed by a left curve. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A04
A Railroad Crossing warning indicates a rail crossing ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A04
At a School Ahead warning, slow down and watch for children at any time. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A04
A Loose Gravel warning indicates loose gravel on the highway ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A04
A One Lane Bridge warning means there is no room to meet or pass another car or truck on the bridge. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A04
A Range Cattle warning indicates that cattle or horses may be on an unfenced highway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A04
A Road Narrows warning indicates a narrower road ahead that still leaves room to meet and pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A04
An Icy Road sign warns that the road is icy and dangerous. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A04
At a School Bus Stop Ahead warning, begin reducing speed for the approaching bus stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F39 | anchor: A04
A Stop Ahead warning calls for beginning to slow for the approaching stop sign. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F40 | anchor: A04
A right-curve warning may carry a suggested safe curve speed below it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

Misconceptions: An advance crossing warning and a sign marking the crossing itself have different instructions; suggested curve speed is distinct from a posted maximum.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: identify the sign, read its instruction, then apply the stated condition.
Glossary: Regulatory sign; warning sign; information-guide sign; barricade; flagger; school zone.
Dynamic facts: Specific local school-zone boundaries, posted speeds and work-zone speed settings vary; use the displayed controls rather than inventing a universal limit.
